body:
#2014 (TASK-1298) REVIEWED, not merged — the drive owns it at phase 2. All six criteria met, and one part is stronger than what I asked for.

THE THRESHOLD SCALES WITH THE WORK AHEAD, which was the point of criterion 1 and the easiest thing to get wrong. `thresholds(hours, lanes, specs)` and `decide_capacity` are both pure, so the policy is adjustable and testable without arranging a full disk.

THE REMEDIES ARE THE PART THAT MAKES IT USEFUL. I asked that a failure name the action rather than the number; these name the shortfall, the path AND the command. Two of them are tonight stated as prevention: "rebuild the selected binary and re-run `aida dev activate`; do not rely on PATH fallback" is the exact incident, and "inspect earlyoom policy rather than disabling it" pre-empts the obvious wrong fix. That last one only gets written by someone who imagined the reader reaching for it.

STRONGER THAN ASKED: I wanted it runnable on demand and NAMED in the procedure before an unattended window. It is wired into `burndown run` as a hard preflight. A step named in a procedure depends on someone following the procedure; a gate does not. That is the substrate-as-bouncer move applied to my own spec, and it is right.

I CHECKED THE THRESHOLDS AGAINST THIS MACHINE, because it now gates launches and a threshold that refuses on the only machine we run on would be worse than no gate:

  thresholds(20h, 4 lanes, 20 specs)  ->  82 GiB disk, 10 GiB memory
  this machine                        ->  204 GiB free, 70 GiB total / 54 available

Comfortable, and correctly calibrated: at 16 KiB free earlier tonight it would have refused. Given the workspace build directory alone reached 121 GiB, an 82 GiB ask for an overnight four-lane run is defensible rather than conservative.

ONE THING TO WATCH, not a change request: `sysinfo` is a new dependency. Reasonable for portable disk and memory reads, and better than hand-rolled platform parsing — but worth someone confirming it builds on the Windows and macOS legs, since this workspace already has foreign-C trouble with `ring` and SQLite. The nightly will answer it, and I would rather flag it now than have it surface as a mystery cross-platform failure next week.

That is the second spec tonight that came back implemented better than I specified it — the first was the CI hint, where a run it could not resolve says so rather than guessing. Both times the improvement was in what the thing does when it CANNOT do its job, which is the part I keep writing as an afterthought and they keep treating as the main case.
